lessons.title: How Smart Casts Work (and Where They Break)
lessons.content: The compiler smart-casts a nullable/sealed type after a check (like `if (x != null)` or `is SomeType`) only when it can prove the value can't change between the check and the use - which is why smart casts fail on `var` properties of a class (another thread could mutate it) but work fine on local `val`s. This is a very common real interview question: why does `if (this.field != null) { use(field) }` sometimes fail to smart-cast inside a class, even though it compiles fine for a local variable.

lessons.title: Writing Your Own Contracts
lessons.content: The `contract { }` block (from kotlin.contracts, still experimental API) lets you tell the compiler about the effects of your own functions, so it can smart-cast based on your custom validation function the same way it does for built-in ones like `requireNotNull`. Real scenario: writing your own `isValidUser(user)` check and having the compiler smart-cast `user` as non-null afterward, just like `checkNotNull` does.
